_comment: JEXI MCP server registry (AGI Phase 2, expanded Sept 2026). permissions are the server's granted boundary: READ_ONLY, LOCAL_WRITE, NETWORK, EXECUTION, GIT, DEPLOYMENT, DESTRUCTIVE. trustLevel: curated (reviewed for JEXI) | community (reviewed upstream only). enabled=true means Lewis switched it on — the gateway connects lazily/on-demand so idle servers cost no memory. Servers needing uvx (Python) or a Chromium download stay disabled with an honest note.

servers.name: filesystem
servers.description: Official MCP reference server — bounded file access with allowlisted roots (read and write within roots only).
servers.notes: Roots must be set to the JEXI workspace, never the home directory. ${JEXI_WORKSPACE} is interpolated at connect time.

servers.name: memory
servers.description: Official MCP reference server — knowledge-graph memory (entities and relations). Studied as a cross-check on JEXI's own memory design.
servers.notes: Optional; JEXI's own WorldModel + memory layers remain the primary memory.

servers.name: everything
servers.description: Official MCP test server — exercises the full MCP protocol (tools, resources, prompts, sampling, roots). Used to verify JEXI's client implementation against the reference implementation.
servers.notes: Test/diagnostic server from the official SDK team; its echo tools prove real round-trips.

servers.name: sequentialthinking
servers.description: Official MCP reference server — structured step-by-step thinking with branching and revision history.
servers.notes: Pure computation, no I/O. A thinking scratchpad JEXI can call like any other tool. (npm name has the hyphen: server-sequential-thinking.)

servers.name: context7
servers.description: Upstash's Context7 — current, version-specific library and framework docs on demand (resolve a library, pull its real docs instead of stale training-data memories).
servers.notes: MIT, maintained by Upstash (~15k stars). Free tier needs NO API key (key only raises rate limits). Read-only docs tools; a hosted streamable-http endpoint (mcp.context7.com/mcp) exists as fallback.

servers.name: fetch
servers.description: Official MCP reference server (Python) — URL to markdown fetching with size and timeout limits.
servers.notes: NEEDS uvx (Python). Not installed on the current host — will not connect until Python/uv is available. JEXI's native deep-read covers this meanwhile.

servers.name: sqlite
servers.description: Official MCP reference server (Python) — read-mostly SQL queries over SQLite databases.
servers.notes: NEEDS uvx (Python). Not installed on the current host. JEXI data lives in JSON; SQL analysis is the genuine gap this would fill. ${JEXI_SQLITE_DB} is interpolated at connect time.

servers.name: time
servers.description: Official MCP reference server (Python) — current time and timezone conversion.
servers.notes: NEEDS uvx (Python). Not installed on the current host. JEXI's own clock covers basic needs meanwhile.

servers.name: playwright
servers.description: Microsoft's Playwright MCP server — browser automation through the MCP standard.
servers.notes: Disabled: needs browser binaries, and JEXI's native browser path is already proven. Flip on only for cross-checks.

servers.name: puppeteer
servers.description: Official MCP reference server — browser automation via Puppeteer.
servers.notes: DISABLED on purpose: installs/downloads a full Chromium (heavy). Redundant with JEXI's native browser control. Flip on only if specifically wanted.

servers.name: brave-search
servers.description: Community MCP server — web search via the Brave Search API.
servers.notes: DISABLED: requires a BRAVE_API_KEY (paid tier for real use). Registered so the slot exists; will not connect without a key.
